question.text: Mr. Ramesh Iyer, CIO of Aravalli Long-Short Fund (a Cat III AIF), is comparing the benchmark characteristics of BSE Sensex 30 (free-float market-cap weighted) with the hypothetical Dow-style price-weighted construct. For a long-short strategy hedged against Sensex, which property of the free-float VALUE-weighted methodology is MOST relevant to his hedge construction?

answer.text: A high-priced constituent exerts disproportionate influence on the index even if its market cap is small
A specified percentage change in a large-cap constituent has a greater index impact than the same percentage change in a small-cap constituent, and stock splits auto-adjust
Each constituent contributes the same percentage weight, irrespective of price or market capitalisation
The weights are assigned based on last-year sales or book value of the issuer, reducing overvaluation bias

explanation.text: The Logic: Under value-weighted (free-float market-cap) construction, weight = security market cap / sum of market caps. A % change in a large-cap therefore moves the index more than the same % change in a small-cap, and stock splits/bonuses auto-adjust because market cap is invariant to splits. This is exactly why Sensex and Nifty 50 (value-weighted) are preferred for index-fund replication and derivative hedging by a Cat III long-short desk. The Trap: Option A describes the pitfall of a PRICE-weighted index (DJIA-style) — a INR 5,000 stock dominates a INR 50 stock by price, not economic size. Option C describes EQUAL-weighted indices (rupee-equal exposure). Option D describes FUNDAMENTAL-weighted indices (sales/book-value/earnings). Only Option B captures the value-weighted property the CIO needs for a Sensex hedge overlay. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B (PM) tests the same index methodology distinction for PMS benchmarking. XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) covers it for both tracks. For Cat I/II benchmarks (XIX-D), PME / KS-PME is used instead — not relevant for Cat III hedge-fund benchmarking which uses market-index returns. Manager's Pro-Tip: For a Cat III long-short desk hedging beta with Sensex futures, remember Sensex is free-float market-cap weighted — so your futures delta mirrors free-float exposure of the top 30 names. If your long book is equal-weighted across 50 mid-caps, Sensex futures will only imperfectly hedge the tail — consider Nifty Midcap 150 futures for residual basis-risk reduction.
